behavior.representative_behavior: At runtime, when a log message containing a JNDI lookup pattern is processed, Log4j interprets the pattern, initiates a remote JNDI lookup via LDAP to attacker.com, retrieves and deserializes attacker-controlled Java class data, and executes the code on the server, resulting in remote code execution.

During HTTP request processing at runtime, the code evaluates user-supplied HTTP parameters as OGNL expressions, which allows arbitrary system command execution by passing malicious payloads, resulting in the attacker gaining remote code execution on the server.

During installation (postinstall), the code executes a shell command to download and run a remote shell script from an external domain, resulting in the installation of a crypto-miner and/or password-stealing malware.
behavior.unified_explanation: remote code execution; install-time execution; command execution; credential theft

behavior.representative_behavior: At runtime, the code establishes a covert outbound connection to a remote command and control server, receives and executes attacker-supplied commands on the host system, and exfiltrates sensitive data via the established channel, resulting in persistent unauthorized remote access and data theft.
behavior.unified_explanation: data exfiltration; backdoor / C2; remote code execution; persistence; credential theft

behavior.representative_behavior: At runtime, after encrypting files, the code writes a ransom note file containing payment instructions to every affected directory, resulting in the victim being informed of the extortion demand.
At import-time, the code accesses the DISCORD_TOKEN environment variable and sends its value to a hardcoded external domain via HTTPS POST, resulting in credential exfiltration.
behavior.unified_explanation: data exfiltration; credential theft; reconnaissance / system info

behavior.representative_behavior: During installation, the code reads the user's ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.aws/credentials files and sends their contents via HTTPS POST to https://malicious.example.com/upload, resulting in credential exfiltration.
behavior.unified_explanation: data exfiltration; credential theft; install-time execution

behavior.representative_behavior: During installation, the code reads the user's ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config files, then sends their contents via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com, resulting in credential exfiltration.
behavior.unified_explanation: data exfiltration; credential theft; install-time execution
